Nrl Energy Station Nazira @ Basanta ... vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 28 November, 2019 Author: Prasanta Kumar Deka Bench: Prasanta Kumar Deka Page No.# 1/6 Gahc010079852019 The Gauhati High Court (High Court Of Assam, Nagaland, Mizoram And Arunachal Pradesh) Case No. : Wp(C) 2488/2019 1: M/S. Nrl Energy Station Nazira @ Basanta Energy Station Situated At Amolapatty, At Road, Nazira, Ward No. Iii, P.O- Nazira, P.S- Nazira, Dist- Sivasagar, Assam, Rep. By Its Sole Prop Namely Minoti Bezbaruah, W/O- Harendra Nath Bezbaruah, R/O- Ongc Colony, Bambobari, P.O- Nazira, P.S- Nazira, Dist- Sivasagar, Assam, Pin- 785685 Versus 1:The State Of Assam And 4 Ors Rep. By The Commissioner And Secretary To The Govt Of Assam, Food And Civil Supply, Dispur, Pin- 781006 2:The Deputy Commissioner Sivasagar Assam Pin- 785640 3:The Sub Divisional Magistrate Nazira Cum Additional Deputy Commissioner Nazira Dist- Sivasagar Assam Pin- 785685 4:The Inspector Food And Civil Suppliers Consumer Affairs Nazira District- Sivasagar Assam Pin- 785685 M/S. texts.facts: The petitioner was licensed by Bharat Petroleum Corporation Limited (BPCL) and on the basis of the said licence she was running her petrol depot at Nazira. M/s BPCL through its engineering department directed its registered vendor M/s NK Enterprise for carrying out modifications and upgradation of the tank and other works in respect of the said petrol depot, M/s NRL Energy Station. After completion of the said work necessary standardisation of the dispensers and the readings of the meters thereof dispensing petrol in the said depot was carried out by the Metrology department at Sivasagar and to that effect a certificate was issued in favour of the petitioner. On 26.07.2018 the Sub-Divisional Magistrate cum Additional Deputy Commissioner, Nazira Sub-Division sealed the petrol dispensers of three dispensing units for investigation/corrective measures. On 14.08.2018 the Forensic Science Laboratory (FSL), Guwahati submitted the analytical report of the samples of the said petrol depot opining about water contents present in the said samples. On 08.09.2018 the Inspector of Food & Civil Supplies Consumer Affairs, Nazira lodged an FIR against the petitioner before the Nazira Police Station. The Nazira Police seized two documents which includes the forwarding report and the analysis report of the FSL, Guwahati. On 13.12.2018 the Nazira police submitted charge-sheet before the court of Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Nazira. It would not be out of place to mention here that M/s BPCL through its letter dated 15.09.2018 Page No.# 3/6 informed the petitioner the cause of presence of water in the sample examined by the FSL, Guwahati as follows:- "To The Dealer, M/s Basanta Energy Station, (M/s NRL Energy Station Nazira) Nazira, Assam Subject: Water entry into underground tank of MS at the retail outlet. Dear Madam, This is to inform you that BPCL, through its engineering Department, M/S. Nrl Energy Station Nazira @ Basanta ... vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 28 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151507030/ 2 had allotted a work order No 4506838572 dated 14.06.2018 to our registered vendor M/s NK Enterprise, for carrying out modifications and upgradations to the tank and pipelines of the retail outlet. While the work was being carried out, due to issue in tank gaskets, water entered the underground tank. If water seeps into the tank for any reason whatsoever, since it is heavier than the petroleum product, it will settle at the bottom of the tank. On suction from the pump, which is from the lower end of the tank, the water is likely to enter the vehicles of the customers. In line with this an incident occurred in the month of July wherein water had entered the underground tank in the retail outlet. Adequate steps have been taken thereafter to rectify the defect and remove the water from the tank. You are also advised to periodically check for water accumulation in underground tank using water detecting paste while checking the dips to avoid incidents in future. Regards, Sd/- P Mahanta Territory Manager (Retail) BPCL, Guwahati" The said action on the part of the respondents is challenged before this court in this writ petition stating that the impugned action is without jurisdiction and in contravention of the Essential Commodities Act, 1955 and the Assam Trade Article (Licence and Control) Order, 1982. The respondent no. 4, the Inspector, Food and Civil Supplies Consumer Affairs Page No.# 4/6 department filed affidavit-in-opposition wherein it is stated that M/s BPCL vide its letter dated 14.08.2018 through its Manager, Sales (Retail), Guwahati informed the Additional Deputy Commissioner cum Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Nazira about the inspection of the depot and the cause of accumulation of water in the underground tank due to seepage during heavy rain and faulty fittings in the tank manhole and the rectifications thereon. The Additional Deputy Commissioner cum Sub-Divisional Magistrate, Nazira vide its letter dated 26.07.2018 requested the Manager (Sales) to carry out a joint inspection/ verification of the depot to settle the issue but there was no response from the said M/s BPCL. Subsequent thereto on 08.09.2018 after receipt of the FSL report opining that the samples failed to meet the BIS specifications for Motor Spirit, FIR was lodged at Nazira Police Station. Since then the matter is under the judicial authority and as such the question of reopening of the sealed depot by the Additional Deputy Commissioner cum Sub-Divisional Judicial Magistrate, Nazira does not arise. In the said affidavit-in-opposition the respondent deponent stated that only the petrol dispensers were sealed but the same were not in the mere opinion of the respondent officials but due to admission of the petitioner about the existence of impurities in the dispensed petrol. Mr. Choudhury submits that on the basis of the FIR, Nazira Police Station charge- sheeted the petitioner as follows:- M/S. Nrl Energy Station Nazira @ Basanta ... vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 28 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151507030/ 3 "Charge or information, Nature of offence and circumstances connected with if so consise detail, and under what section of the Penal code charged. The brief fact of the case is that on 26/07/2018 in the afternoon at around 4 PM, as per verbal complaint received from the public, the informant Md. Kamaluddin Ahmed, Inspector, Food, Civil Supplies & Consumer Affairs, Nazira, has taken samples from M/S Basanta Energy Petrol pump and send it to Gauhati FSL for examination, and after receipt the analysis report from FSL, it is found that the owner of the above petrol pump, Smt Minoti Bezboruah W/O (Lt) Horendra Bezboruah, resident of Nazira ward No 8, of Police station Nazira, and Manager Sri Biju Sarmah, S/O late Nila Kt Sarmah, resident of No - 02 Halaguri Gaon, Police Station - Sivasagar has done adulteration in the above mentioned petrol. Accordingly, the Informant has lodged a First Information Report and FIR was registered under section 7 of Essential Commodities Act and after investigation, I submitted Charge-sheet before this Hon'ble Court. The witnesses mentioned in Column no 6 will prove the truth of the Ejahar. Therefore, it is requested to send summon to the witnesses by fixing the trial day. 1 (one) seizure list, sketch-map, 2(two) bail bonds, FSL report are attached along with the First Information Page No.# 5/6 Report. Along with case diary, sketch map, seizure list, 2 (two) nos Bail Bond and Expert opinion of PSL report are enclosed here with. Sd/- illegible"
texts.arguments: Having not done so, there is a specific violation of the fundamental rights guaranteed under the Constitution of India of the petitioner is apparent and as such he sought for directing the respondents to act as per law by removing the seal of the said dispensers in the petrol pump. Ms. Bhattcharjee submits that the respondent officials within the prescribed jurisdiction under the Assam Trade Article (Licence and Control) Order, 1982 and M/S. Nrl Energy Station Nazira @ Basanta ... vs The State Of Assam And 4 Ors on 28 November, 2019 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/151507030/ 4 the FSL report indicating non compliance of the BIS specifications rightly initiated the action under Clause 4 of the Motor Spirit and High Speed Diesel (Regulation of Supply and Distribution and Prevention of Malpractices) Order, 1998 to protect the interest of the consumers of the petroleum product. In addition to that Ms. Bhattacharjee projected that there is an admission on the part of the petitioner, the licensee under M/s BPCL about the water content which is also one of the grounds for lodging the FIR. However, Ms. Bhattacharjee fairly submits that as the FIR was lodged by the respondent officials for a judicial decision and as the petitioner is discharged there being no challenge to the judicial decision of the learned SDJM, Nazira, the same would hold the field and the consequences thereafter.
